page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-64GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 20 vCPUs and 20 physical cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.2 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core testing placing it in the bottom 10% with a score of 784.29. However, multi-core and parallelized workloads perform significantly better. The stress-ng multi-core test yields an average score of 15708.05, and the bzip3 multi-threaded decompression benchmark registers a strong result in the top 25% at 182.69 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, including read-only large block (69.81 GB/sec) and write large block (29.73 GB/sec), fall consistently within the average tier.

This server is suited for multi-threaded applications that can leverage its 20 shared vCPUs, such as parallel software compilation, text processing, and static web serving. It also demonstrates strong performance in prompt processing for small language models (135M), achieving 2344.1 tokens/sec. However, due to its shared CPU allocation and poor single-core performance, it is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or latency-sensitive workloads that require dedicated, high-frequency CPU cores. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment for persistent data.
